newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian patrol boats, helicopters flee to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albanian patrol boats, helicopters flee to Italy.

text.p: At least two Albanian military helicopters and three torpedo boats were taken to Italy on Thursday, apparently by deserting crews fleeing the Balkan country's slid into anarchy.

The escapes took place as Prime Minister Romano Prodi held an emergency meeting with his defence, interior and foreign ministers to discuss the crisis engulfing Albania, a short distance across the Adriatic from Italy.
Italy also carried out the latest in a series of dramatic evacuations from Albania, rescuing some 400 foreign nationals with helicopters that were ferrying them to Italian warships in the Adriatic.
Diplomatic sources said the evacuees included about 330 Italians and some 70 other foreigners.
In Brindisi, two Albanian air force helicopters with several people on board landed near the southeastern port city, the city's prefect, Andrea Gentile, told Reuters.
The Italian news agency ANSA said a total of 16 people were on the two aircraft, including women and at least one child.
Military sources in Rome said four more helicopters had been sighted heading for southern Italy's Puglia region. "We are monitoring their route," one source said.
Earlier, the Italian navy said three Albanian torpedo boats had deserted in international waters where they raised the white flag of surrender after being sighted by an Italian frigate.
Two of the three boats, all ageing Chinese-built Huchuan class vessels, were being led under escort to Brindisi and the third had entered the port of Bari, the navy said.
A merchant ship that had been seized in the port of Durres with scores of Albanians on board was also heading for Brindisi under an Italian navy escort, coastguards said.
The Albanians aboard that vessel were believed to be armed.

The Italian ferry Palladio left Albania earlier than scheduled on Thursday after order broke down in Durres. The ferry was due to arrive at the port of Bari on Thursday night with about 60 people on board.
Unconfirmed reports said a number of small boats were also on their way across the southern Adriatic with Albanians desperate to escape the chaos in their impoverished country.
Last week, an Albanian military plane landed in southern Italy and its two pilots asked for political asylum.

Italy, which has taken an active role in international efforts to end Albania's deepening chaos, was hit by a wave of some 40,000 Albanians who fled in rusting freighters in 1991 after iron-fisted Stalinist rule collapsed in their country.
It has beefed up security in the southern Adriatic as a result of the latest unrest, sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes in which tens of thousands of Albanians lost their savings.
Albania slid further towards chaos on Thursday as arms depots in several towns including the capital Tirana were looted and people used the weapons to raid food warehouses for emergency stockpiles.
